Report what you have now, partial is fine — and note the branch moved under you.

When I spawned you, `fix/spawn-binding` HEAD was `fbb2ea8`. It is now `f9bbf00`, seven commits later. The third reviewer (silent-failure) already delivered and its findings have been fixed, so if you were reading the working tree rather than a pinned diff, some of what you are looking at has changed beneath you. That is my scoping error, not yours.

What landed since you started, so you can tell which of your findings are already closed:

- Pending-dispatch match/block messages now name the pending binding as the source and `ethos mission release` as the remedy, instead of blaming `MISSION_ID`.
- `HandleSessionEnd` now clears the delegation-binding sidecar too.
- `sort.Slice` → stable sort with a mission-ID tiebreak; `ReadDispatchPending` now rejects symlinks.
- `abandon --disclaim` now names which disclaims were committed when `Abandon` subsequently fails.
- A crashed-write delegation directory now yields an error naming the remedy instead of an opaque "file does not exist".
- `ReadActiveMissionBinding` gained a `BindOriginUnknown` sentinel: an origin file that exists but does not resolve is no longer answered as `claim`.
- `matchDispatchPending` now skips and clears provably-non-open entries, and holds a per-session exclusive lock across match-through-admit.

**What I most want from you, if you have it:** anything on the `dispatch-pending` store itself and its FIFO matching, `Abandon`'s relaxed gate (`countBlockingDelegations`, the `aborted` exclusion, `DisclaimDelegation`), or `BoundVia` backward compatibility. Those are the newest code and the least reviewed.

If everything you found is in the list above, say so plainly — "no findings beyond what's fixed" is a useful result and I will take it. Do not start over on the new commits; I will commission that separately if needed.

tool_input.message:
Report what you have now, partial is fine — and note the branch moved under you.

When I spawned you, `fix/spawn-binding` HEAD was `fbb2ea8`. It is now `f9bbf00`, seven commits later, and DES-076 has been amended again. If you were reading the working tree rather than a pinned diff, the ADR text you are verifying has changed beneath you. My scoping error, not yours.

Relevant to your six claims specifically:

- **Claim 1 (C2 closed structurally):** since strengthened. `ReadActiveMissionBinding` gained a `BindOriginUnknown` sentinel — an origin file that EXISTS but does not cleanly resolve (truncated, or naming a different mission) no longer answers `claim`. Absence still answers `claim` as the legacy-safe case. So the read-side default itself changed, not just the write paths.
- **Claim 2 (FIFO ordering):** `sort.Slice` was not stable; now a stable sort with a mission-ID tiebreak. Ambiguity is now signalled to stderr naming the competing missions and the `MISSION_ID` override. And `matchDispatchPending` now skips and clears provably-non-open entries — a stale entry was previously head-of-line-blocking every newer pending dispatch for the same worker.
- **New since you started:** a per-session exclusive lock across match-through-admit, because two concurrent `Agent()` spawns in one turn could both match the same entry. This org's conventions call for batching independent tool calls, so that was the normal path.
- **Claim 4 (session end):** now also clears the delegation-binding sidecar, which it previously omitted while claiming to clear everything `release` clears.

**What I most want from you:** your verdict on **claim 6 — the residual-risk section's completeness**. That is the highest-value part of your review and the reason I commissioned you specifically. The previous version of this ADR under-stated what it left open, and three defects survived a full review round because readers trusted it. If the current residual list is still incomplete, that finding is worth more than the rest combined.

Second priority: your test-quality assessment. You previously caught a test that existed to prove one binding type never converts to another and checked only the field that does not change under that conversion. If that shape recurs in the new tests, I want it.

If everything you found is already in the list above, say so plainly — "no findings beyond what's fixed" is a useful result. Do not start over on the new commits.

tool_input.message:
Both remaining reviewers landed. **They reviewed `fbb2ea8`, so a lot of what they found you already fixed in `ab3e8dc`..`f9bbf00`.** I've separated it so you don't redo work.

**Already closed — confirmed, do not revisit:** concurrent-spawn race (your F3 lock), session-end delegation-binding (b61fe9c), mtime ties (a42a2be), unreadable-record comment (cb72c5f), `BindOriginDispatch` doc block, `warnNonOpenMissionID`'s boundVia-switched messages, and the non-open head-of-line block (your F2). Both reviewers independently verified your `BoundVia` backward-compat reasoning, the disclaim locking/rollback discipline, the gate-2 separation, and the aborted-exclusion safety argument — one enumerated all three `DelegationVerdictAborted` writers and confirmed the third is unreachable because nothing returns a contract to `StatusOpen`. That work is solid.

**Eleven still open. Two critical.**

---

**K1 — CRITICAL. Your F2 fix closed the non-open case but the unloadable-contract case still poisons the queue permanently.**

You skip and clear entries you can *prove* non-open, and defer unresolvable ones to `dispatchTierB` per C3's doctrine. Right instinct on not deleting for unproven reasons — but the consequence is that an entry whose contract won't load sits at the head forever and **every** matching spawn is denied. Reviewer proved it: three consecutive `bwk` spawns, all denied, entry still there.

Reachable without exotic faults: mission contracts are git-tracked, so `mission dispatch` then `git checkout` removes `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/<id>/` and walls off that agent type for the session.

Your H1 fix means the message now names `ethos mission release`, which makes it recoverable — real improvement. But a newer, perfectly valid pending entry for the same worker is still unreachable behind the stuck one. **Skip it in `matchDispatchPending` and continue to the next matching entry — do not delete it** (C3's doctrine stands: a Load failure proves nothing, and the contract may come back on the next branch switch). Warn naming the skipped mission and the remedy. That way an unresolvable head never blocks a queue, and nothing is destroyed on unproven evidence.

**K2 — CRITICAL. The abandon doc of record and the guide shipped to every consuming repo still describe the pre-DES-076 gate. I verified both.**

`docs/mission-abandon.md:42-56`: *"Zero entries exist … at any verdict. Any entry — even one that already closed pass or fail — proves a worker was actually spawned"* and *"There is no override flag, for the same reason `close` has none: the gate is the whole point."* Both false now — `verdict == aborted` is excluded, and `--disclaim` exists. The "why the check is on existence, not verdict" section is now backwards.

`internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md:33`: *"Refuses if any delegation or result exists."* **That file is deposited into every repo that runs `ethos enable`** — it's what a downstream agent reads before choosing abandon vs close. Shipping a false gate description there is worse than shipping it here.

Definition of Done item 5 requires user-facing docs in the PR diff. Update both.

---

**K3 — HIGH. A pending dispatch survives abnormal session death, and the CHANGELOG claims otherwise unconditionally.** `Store.Delete` removes only the roster YAML; nothing touches the `sessions/<id>/` sidecar directory. So your C6 fix covers the clean SessionEnd path only. SIGKILL, a closed terminal, or a crash leaves the entry indefinitely — no GC, no purge, no tombstone path. `claude --resume` then reuses the ID and the first matching spawn is captured. The CHANGELOG says resume "no longer inherits a stale claim or pending dispatch," full stop. Either add sidecar cleanup to the purge/tombstone path or age entries out by `CreatedAt` (you already read it) — and soften the CHANGELOG to "ended cleanly" regardless.

**K4 — HIGH. The aborted-exclusion's safety rests on "exactly three writers" with nothing enforcing it.** Both reviewers verified the invariant holds *today*. But `CloseDelegationSkeleton` is exported and takes any verdict string; the day someone adds a fourth pre-`Close` writer — a "cancel a running worker" command is the obvious one — a delegation whose worker did real work silently stops blocking abandon, with no reason, no event, no attestation. That's exactly the class you've been catching: true today, structurally unenforced, comment reading as guarantee. Add a drift-guard test that enumerates `DelegationVerdictAborted` write sites and fails on any count but the known three — `internal/mcpclass` already does this discipline. Not a comment.

**K5 — HIGH. `cmd/ethos/mission.go:346` still says "at any verdict"** in user-facing `--help`, and `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go:25` says "refuses if any non-disclaimed delegation record exists." Both wrong — aborted is excluded *unconditionally, independent of disclaim*. An operator whose only delegation was depth-refused is told to find a `--disclaim` they don't need.

**K6 — HIGH. No CHANGELOG entry for the aborted-verdict gate loosening.** I grepped: no `[Unreleased]` line covers it. A mission whose only delegations were depth- or hash-refused can now be abandoned with no `--disclaim` at all. That's a safety-gate relaxation and the repo requires the entry in the diff.

**K7 — HIGH, two parts, on your own C2 fix.** (a) `DESIGN.md:9762-9769` still says the ADR "does not claim to have inverted the reader's failure direction… there is no longer a decision to invert." Your `BindOriginUnknown` change *does* invert it. The ADR now describes a design that doesn't exist. (b) Your new tests cover **truncated and mismatched** origin files — but the shape that actually exists in the field is a *well-formed* legacy dispatch pair, written by the currently-released `bindDispatchedMission` and sitting on disk right now for every ethos user. On upgrade, that pair must be refused. Add a hook-level test staging `WriteActiveMissionOrigin(..., BindOriginDispatch)` and asserting the spawn is not captured. The reviewer found your fix *by probing for this*, and the probe passed — but nothing pins it.

---

**K8 — MEDIUM.** `cmd/ethos/mission.go:2150-2156` and the MCP twin still print *"will attribute worker %q's next matching Agent() spawn to %s"* unconditionally. When a pending entry for that worker already exists, that's false — the next matching spawn goes to the *older* mission. Your `matchDispatchPending` warning fires at spawn time; this one is wrong at dispatch time. Read the pending store before writing and name the queue position.

**K9 — MEDIUM, prose.** `DESIGN.md:9955` says out-of-order spawning misattributes "m-B's spawn to m-A." It's symmetric: A's entry is consumed by B's spawn, so A's own later spawn then matches B. Two misattributions per out-of-order pair — the same doubling you spell out explicitly for C1.

**K10 — MEDIUM, prose.** The security review enumerates hand-editing `bound_via` to unlock disclaim. Hand-editing `verdict: aborted` is a second unlock of the same gate and is *strictly worse* — disclaim leaves a record on the delegation and an event-log entry; a hand-edited verdict leaves nothing. Name it, given you named the weaker sibling.

**K11 — MEDIUM, tests guarding fixtures rather than properties.** (a) `..._ClaimOrigin_StaysAfterConsume` — this is the third time this exact shape has come up. It exists to prove a claim binding never converts to a dispatch binding, and asserts only `ReadActiveMission == missionID`, the field that survives *both* shapes. Round 1's F6 made the dispatch-side mirror assert `Origin`; the claim side was never made symmetric. (b) `TestStore_Abandon_SucceedsAfterDepthRefusalWithNoDisclaim` — DESIGN.md calls it "the end-to-end proof using the real depth-refusal shape," but it hand-calls `CloseDelegationSkeleton`; its own comment says "simulate." If `closeDelegationAborted` stopped closing the skeleton, C7 regresses and this stays green. Drive it through `HandlePreToolUse` with depth exceeded, or drop "end-to-end" from the ADR.

---

Your call on K1's mechanism — I've stated what I want but you know the doctrine constraints better. Everything else is straightforward. Same gates, same falsification discipline, don't push.
